topicName: Kanban Method Principles and Flow Metrics
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Kanban Method Principles and Flow Metrics"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Kanban"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kanban is an Agile method used to visualize work, limit work-in-progress (WIP), and maximize efficiency (or flow). Unlike Scrum, which relies on fixed-length iterations, Kanban focuses on continuous delivery and adapting to capacity constraints dynamically."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"The Core Principles of Kanban"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Kanban method is divided into two categories: Change Management Principles and Service Delivery Principles. Here are the foundational change management principles:"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Start with what you do now: Understand current processes, job roles, and workflows without disrupting existing structures."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Agree to pursue incremental, evolutionary change: Small, continuous improvements are encouraged to minimize resistance to change."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Respect the current process, roles, and responsibilities: Avoid making sweeping changes immediately; respect existing organizational design."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Encourage acts of leadership at all levels: Cultivate continuous improvement from individual contributors, not just management."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Essential Flow Metrics"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"To measure and optimize system performance, Kanban relies heavily on flow metrics. These metrics help teams forecast delivery times and spot bottlenecks."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"WIP (Work in Progress): The total number of items currently in progress between the started and finished states."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Lead Time: The total time elapsed from the moment a request is made until it is delivered to the customer."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cycle Time: The time it takes for a work item to travel from the \"In Progress\" state to the \"Done\" state."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Throughput: The number of work items processed and completed per unit of time (e.g., items per week)."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Little's Law in Kanban"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Little's Law is a foundational mathematical formula used in flow-based systems. It states that the average number of items in a queuing system (WIP) is equal to the average arrival rate (Throughput) multiplied by the average time an item spends in the system (Lead Time)."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"WIP = Throughput * Lead Time"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"By rearranging this formula, if your WIP increases while throughput remains constant, your lead time will inherently increase. Therefore, controlling WIP is the primary mechanism for accelerating delivery."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering Kanban principles and analyzing flow metrics allows Agile teams to transition from guesswork to predictable, data-driven delivery. Focus on limiting WIP, visualizing constraints, and optimizing flow continuously."}]
